description: Somos un equipo multidisciplinario enfocado en transformar la agricultura de precisión mediante la física y la ciencia de datos. Fusionamos observaciones de la Tierra de la NASA con un modelo dinámico de espacios de fases y firmas bioclimáticas por especie, creando soluciones inteligentes que ayudan a los agricultores a anticipar el estrés climático y diseñar estrategias de rotación altamente resilientes para proteger la salud del suelo a largo plazo.
summary:
We developed AgroPhasor, a physics-driven agricultural digital twin powered by a 5-variable coupled differential equation engine (modeling thermodynamics, hydrology, N-P-K nutrients, biomass, and erosion) with closed-form analytical solutions. Currently at a functional prototype stage, AgroPhasor renders selected farmland as interactive 30m × 30m 3D grid cells with real elevation variations, showing how uneven slopes shape microclimates rather than assuming flat terrain. Choosing a plant generates a Dynamic Resilience Shield over the parcel that shifts from deep blue (high resistance) to red (low resistance) based on crop physiology, while a top timeline bar lets users scrub through the hours of the day to track intraday climate stress.

AgroPhasor addresses the climate resilience challenge by fusing orbital datasets (NASA POWER, SRTM, Sentinel-2) into an intuitive visual simulator, laying the foundation for multi-year crop rotation optimization. This matters because farmers and researchers do not need to decipher complex spreadsheets to protect yields; they can visually test how terrain slope, daily solar cycles, and crop genetics interact to prevent crop failure and build sustainable farms.
details:
AgroPhasor is a physics-driven agricultural digital twin powered by five coupled differential equations—modeling canopy thermodynamics, hydrology, N-P-K nutrients, biomass, and erosion—solved via exact closed-form analytical equations. Fusing NASA POWER, SRTM elevation, Sentinel-2, and soil APIs with a JSON crop database, our functional prototype renders farmland as interactive 30m × 30m 3D grid cells with real elevation variations. Rather than presenting raw weather spreadsheets, we creatively translated plant biophysics into a Dynamic Resilience Shield over the terrain that shifts from deep blue (high climate resistance) to red (high vulnerability) based on the selected crop, while a top timeline bar lets users scrub through the hours of the day to track intraday stress.

Because analytical solutions eliminate slow numerical solvers, AgroPhasor runs smoothly on standard laptops and browsers without specialized hardware. While the Monte Carlo climate forecaster and multi-year rotation optimizer have not been integrated into the live build yet, this prototype establishes the core physics engine required to power them next. Our intended impact is to help farmers and researchers prevent climate-driven yield losses, curb slope erosion, and design sustainable rotations. To keep the model realistic, we factored in terrain slope and altitude lapse rates, botanical family rules against pests, single- and multi-harvest crop lifecycles, tillage erosion spikes, and automatic fallbacks for missing soil data. We built the simulation backend in Python and the interactive frontend using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
